summary.text: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, usually called the Moho, is the boundary between Earth's crust and its mantle.
It is marked by a jump in seismic wave speed of about 1 km/s, as waves pass from basalt-like rock above into peridotite-like rock below.
Croatian seismologist Andrija Mohorovičić identified it in 1909 after noticing two sets of earthquake waves, one refracted by a faster layer beneath.

facts.label: Depth under oceans
facts.value: 5 to 10 km below the ocean floor

facts.label: Depth under continents
facts.value: 20 to 90 km, about 35 km on average

items.prompt: Project Mohole tried to drill down to the Moho from deep-ocean regions instead of from dry land. Why does that choice make sense?

options.label: Ocean rock is softer to drill
The Moho is much shallower under the seafloor
Seawater keeps the drill cool
Land drilling was banned by treaty

items.explain: The Moho lies only 5 to 10 km below the ocean floor, but 20 to 90 km beneath continents.

items.prompt: An earthquake wave travels down out of the crust and into the mantle. What happens to its speed as it crosses the Moho?

options.label: It slows down sharply
It stops completely
It speeds up
It stays exactly the same

items.explain: P-waves travel about 6.7–7.2 km/s just above the Moho and about 7.6–8.6 km/s below it.

items.prompt: Mohorovičić saw two separate sets of waves arrive from a single earthquake. What did he conclude?

options.label: A sharp density change lies deep below
Two earthquakes had struck at once
His instruments were recording echoes
The waves bounced off the ocean surface

items.explain: He reasoned that the second set could only come from a sharp transition in density that changed the waves' speed.

items.prompt: Under slowly spreading mid-ocean ridges, mantle rock can change in a way that slows seismic waves. How does that shift where the Moho shows up?

options.label: It makes the Moho look shallower
It has no effect on the Moho
It makes the Moho disappear upward
It makes the Moho look deeper

items.explain: Serpentinization lowers seismic wave velocities in mantle rock, which can increase the depth to the Moho.

items.prompt: Why must geologists be careful when mapping the crust from seismic data alone?

options.label: Seismic waves cannot reach the mantle
The Moho may sit well below the true crust-mantle boundary
The Moho moves from day to day
Earthquakes erase the boundary they cross

items.explain: Since the 1980s geologists have known the Moho does not always match the boundary defined by rock composition.

items.prompt: Soviet scientists drilled the Kola Superdeep Borehole aiming at the Moho. How far down did they get before giving up?

options.label: About 1.2 km
About 12 km
About 35 km
About 90 km

items.explain: They reached 12,260 metres, the world's deepest hole, before abandoning the project.
